correctness.rationale: In the specified m-triangle open graph each bond belongs to exactly one triangle, so the normalized exchange is −m+4 times the monochromatic-triangle count. At zero field each mixed triangle independently gives three choices conditional on its first base spin, yielding 2·3^m. For 0<x<2 a monochromatic triangle can lower its energy by changing its private tip. The least number of down spins among mixed configurations on any base word is d+u, where d is the count of down bases and u the count of consecutive up-base pairs; this equals the base length L=m+1 minus the number of up runs. At maximal run count, odd L gives the unique up-ended alternating word. Even L=2r has one surplus site beyond the minimum needed for r up runs: it can lengthen one of r up runs or fill one of r+1 down gaps, giving L+1 base words. At x=2 only the tip on an up-up base pair can freely change, gaining two magnetization units for one extra monochromatic triangle. There is none for odd L, and exactly one such pair in each of the r up-run extensions for even L, giving the two stated odd-m sectors. For x>2 the all-up comparison removes all down spins outside the degree-four interior path; an occupied component of length greater than one costs more than its singleton replacement by 2J(x−2) per removed site. For 2<x<4, the maximizing cardinality is floor(m/2), with binomial path counts giving the two degeneracies. At x=4 all independent sets tie; a size-k set has M=2m+1−2k and count binomial(m−k,k), totaling F_(m+1). Above x=4 only the fully polarized state survives. Energies and entropies follow from these reductions; the positive-field 2J crossing is a finite-size distinction, not a claim about a finite-temperature or bulk transition.
residual_risks: Finite replay corroborates but does not replace the all-size proof. Open boundaries and equal antiferromagnetic couplings are essential hypotheses.
